correctness.rationale: Bezout and the maximal reduced intersection make f_x,f_y homogeneous degree-m complete-intersection generators, m=d−1; every degree≤m polynomial vanishing on the critical set lies in their two-dimensional span. Thus a companion has gradient A∇f for a constant nonscalar matrix A. Integrability yields nonzero constant-coefficient second-order PDE c f_xx+(e−a)f_xy−b f_yy=0. Its binary quadratic symbol over C either splits in distinct factors, giving f=F(u)+G(v), or is repeated, giving f=uH(v)+G(v). In the latter case H has ≤m simple roots, so at most m nondegenerate critical points—contradicting m² for m≥2. The distinct case forces full degree d squarefree derivatives, and companion rigidity follows by separation and mixed-partial equality. Small symbolic Hessian checks support but do not replace Bezout and the PDE classification.
